audit.method: Uniform sample (mulberry32, seeded Fisher-Yates) of the ANCHORED findings, each read by hand against its matched diff lines. `verdict` is the NAMING bar (what `anchored` claims): good = the matching anchor refers to the same code entity the comment is about; spurious = a homonym, or not a code reference at all. `localized` is a stricter LOCATION bar: precise = a matched line is the site the comment targets; diffuse = the right entity is named but the target site is never matched.

verdicts.note: `picocli.exit` matched the exact `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult…)` calls the comment names.
`UserModel` matched `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel currentUser)` — the signature under discussion.

Weakest of the 20. `checkPermission` IS the function the comment names, but the one matched line is its production call site; the comment is about a misleading comment + `false` value in the test's cached-permission map, which the anchor never reaches.
`GrafanaRuleListItem` matched both its definition and the `<GrafanaRuleListItem` render site missing the `key` prop.
`applyTemplateVariables` matched the exact three-argument call (`…, request.scopedVars, request.filters`) the comment quotes.
`dbSession.Exec` matched `result, err := dbSession.Exec(args...)` verbatim — the line that would not compile.
`ErrDeviceLimitReached` matched its declaration and the `return ErrDeviceLimitReached` the comment calls misleading.
All three anchors matched: the removed `traceID` logging lines in `LoggerMiddleware` and the new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` that omits them.
`before_validation` matched the `before_validation do` block in embeddable_host.rb; the `EmbeddableHost` anchor added 11 further, unrelated call sites.

Right entity, wrong places: `embeddable_hosts`/`EmbeddableHost` matched 13 lines across 9 files (JS controllers, hbs templates, locale yml) and never the raw-SQL migration the comment is actually about.
`include_website_name` matched `def include_website_name` — literally the method whose missing `?` suffix is the finding.

`postMessage` matched the exact `parent.postMessage(…, '<%= request.referer %>')` line. The separate `URL` anchor matched a locale string and two spec titles — acronym noise inside an otherwise correct label.
`TopicEmbed` matched `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, …)`, the method the comment names; the `HTML` anchor separately matched an unrelated code comment.
`TopicUser` matched `tu = TopicUser.find_by(…)` — the nil-able assignment the comment warns about.
The misspelled `stopNotificiationsText` matched its definition and its template use; the correctly-spelled variant matched nothing, as it should.
Four anchors matched the exact `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset,…) === dayjs(date.end)…` comparison the comment says will always be false.
`immediateDelete` matched `if (immediateDelete) {` inside `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` — the exact branch the comment describes.
`TwoFactor` matched `export default function TwoFactor` inside BackupCode.tsx — the naming inconsistency itself.
`backupCodes` matched the decrypt-then-mutate lines in disable.ts that the race-condition comment is about.
`createEvent`/`credentialId` matched both `Calendar.d.ts` declarations the comment contrasts, plus the implementation that keeps the old arity.
